verifications.claim: Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. EDT
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '8:07 p.m. ET in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California' on 'April 10, 2026'; R2: '8:07 p.m. EDT on Friday, April 10... off the coast of California, possibly near San Diego'; R3: '8:07 p.m. EDT... off the coast of San Diego'; R4: '8:07 p.m. EDT... off the coast of San Diego'; R5: 'April 11, 2026, 00:07:27 UTC (April 10, 5:07:27 p.m. PDT)' southwest of San Diego; R6/R7/R8 confirm splashdown details
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the exact date, time in EDT, and location matching the claim.

verifications.claim: 8:07 p.m. EDT is equivalent to 5:07 p.m. PDT
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '8:07 p.m. EDT (0007GMT)... Splashing down locally at 5:07 pm PDT'; R3: '8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT)'; R4: '8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT)'; R5: 'April 11, 2026, 00:07:27 UTC (April 10, 5:07:27 p.m. PDT)'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly equate 8:07 p.m. EDT to 5:07 p.m. PDT for the splashdown.

verifications.claim: Splashdown completed a 10-day mission around the moon
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'final day of their 10-day milestone mission to orbit the moon'; R2: 'end a 10-day test flight around the moon'; R3: '10-day mission'; R4: 'approximate 10-day mission around the Moon'; R5: '9 days, 1 hour, 32 minutes... crewed lunar flyby'; R6: '10-day mission'
verifications.reasoning: All sources describe the mission as a 10-day journey around the moon completed by splashdown.

verifications.claim: Splashdown initiated recovery process by U.S. Navy and NASA teams
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'U.S. Navy recovery vessel'; R3: 'combined NASA and U.S. military recovery team... extract the crew from Orion'; R4: 'NASA and the U.S. military now are approaching... recovery team aboard the USS John P. Murtha'; R5: 'U.S. Navy recovered the crew'; R6: 'U.S. Navy is assisting with recovery efforts'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm joint NASA/U.S. Navy recovery initiated post-splashdown.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Exact time stated directly in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: Splashdown time was 00:07 UTC on April 11
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Sources specify 00:07 UTC/GMT on April 11, matching exactly.

verifications.claim: Splashdown location was Pacific Ocean near San Diego, California
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R3/R4/R7: 'off the coast of San Diego, California'; R2: 'off the coast of California, possibly near San Diego'; R5: 'Pacific Ocean southwest of San Diego'; R6/R8: 'off California’s coast/off the coast of San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm Pacific Ocean near/off coast of San Diego, CA.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R2/R3/R4/R6: '10-day mission'; R5: '9 days, 1 hour, 32 minutes and 15 seconds' but described as ~10-day
verifications.reasoning: Consistently referred to as 10-day mission; precise duration slightly under but matches common description.

verifications.claim: Mission was a crewed lunar-flyby test flight
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'test flight... to orbit the moon'; R2: '10-day test flight around the moon... crewed mission... flyby of the moon'; R3: 'lunar flyby'; R5: 'crewed lunar flyby mission... test flight'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe as crewed lunar flyby test flight.

verifications.claim: Recovery vessel was USS John P. Murtha
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'fly them via helicopter to the USS John P. Murtha'; R4: 'USS John P. Murtha'; R5: 'Recovered by USS John P. Murtha'; R6: 'USS John P. Murtha'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources name USS John P. Murtha as recovery vessel.

verifications.claim: Crewed capsule re-entered Earth's atmosphere at approximately 7:53 p.m. EDT
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '7:53 p.m.: Entry interface'; R2: '7:53 p.m. EDT: Entry Interface'; R3: '7:53 p.m.: ... Entry interface'; R4: '7:53 p.m. The Orion spacecraft reached Earth’s atmosphere'
verifications.reasoning: Entry interface (re-entry) precisely at 7:53 p.m. EDT in sources.

verifications.claim: Crewed capsule experienced a 6-minute communication blackout before deploying parachutes
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: '7:53 p.m.... planned six-minute communications blackout... 8:03 p.m.: ... drogue parachutes will deploy'; R4: '7:53 p.m.... planned communications blackout... 8:00 p.m. NASA has reestablished communications... 8:03 p.m. ... drogue parachutes'
verifications.reasoning: Sources detail ~6-min blackout starting at entry (7:53), ending before parachutes (8:03).

verifications.claim: Parachutes deployed for final 8:07 p.m. landing
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '8:07 p.m.: Splashdown'; timeline with parachutes prior; R3: '8:03 p.m.: drogue parachutes... 8:04 p.m.: three main parachutes... 8:07 p.m.: Splashdown'; R4: '8:03 p.m.... drogue parachutes... 8:04 p.m.... three main parachutes... 8:07 p.m. SPLASHDOWN'
verifications.reasoning: Parachutes deployed just before 8:07 p.m. splashdown/landing as described.
